correctness.rationale: Affine barycentric columns have a zero at their own facet index and are Dirichlet(1,…,1) on the remaining n-1 entries. The normalized oriented volume is the determinant. The mean determinant follows from multilinearity and the spectrum of (J-I)/(n-1). For the square, independence allows replacing the random rank-one column outer products by their means in the squarefree coefficient only. Scaling by n(n-1), the summed moment matrix has diagonal 2(T-t_i) and off-diagonal T-t_i-t_j. A rank-two update of TI gives nT^(n-2)(T²-∑t_i²): in the 2×2 reduction the diagonal is (n,0) and the off-diagonals are (T²-∑t_i²)/T and -n/T. Only T^n contributes to the required squarefree coefficient, giving n n!, even at n=2. The interior moment comes from n! det((I+J)/(n(n+1))); the exact ratio tends to e², and its square root tends to e. Squaring the signed determinant expansion gives precisely the derangement sum by the 2:1 ratio of repeated-entry to distinct-entry moments. The n=2 transposition and n=3 positive derangement terms give the stated signs; at n=4 and n=5 both parities occur and adding disjoint transpositions extends to all higher n. Permutation matrices are limit points with positive-probability relative neighborhoods of constant sign. The variance follows from the two moments, not from any claim about the unsigned first moment.
residual_risks: The checker alone is finite; the squarefree determinant argument is the all-dimensional proof. No sign probabilities at n≥4 or unsigned first moments were validated.

originality.rationale: A distinct same-date Resultary theorem explicitly states the exact shape-independent opposite-facet moment with the identical law for every nontrivial dimension. Its scope is bigger on boundary sampling. The interior e² ratio and signed derangement expansion are direct implications using known iid covariance and the entry second moments; n=2 is deterministic. This establishes material equivalent coverage, not which same-day work appeared first. The other signed statistics are elementary consequences of the same model, not a surviving distinct main result.
residual_risks: Calendar date alone does not establish which same-date result preceded the other. Earlier equivalent results under different matrix or simplex nomenclature may exist; the established overlap does not rely on those possibilities.
